title: Walking in the Park Vocabulary
summary: A sunny walk in the park: stretch, jog, sprint, take a break, catch your breath.
script:
Imagine yourself in a beautiful park.
It's a beautiful sunny day.
Before you start moving, you stretch your body.
You lift your arms above your head and stretch.
To stretch means to move your body or part of your body to make your muscles longer and more relaxed.
Now, you start to walk along a quiet path. You walk slowly, one step at a time.
You look around and notice the trees, the grass, and the flowers around you.
After walking for a while, you decide to move a little faster. You start to jog.
To jog means to run slowly, usually for exercise.
Now, imagine going a little faster. You start to run.
You run past the trees and feel the fresh air on your face.
And for just a few seconds, you sprint.
To sprint means to run as fast as you can for a short distance.
You sprint…and then you stop.
Your heart is beating faster now, so you find a bench and take a break.
To take a break means to stop what you’re doing for a short time so you can rest.
You sit down and catch your breath.
To catch your breath means to rest for a moment until you can breathe normally again.
You pick up your water bottle and take a sip of water.
A sip is a small amount of a drink.
You sit quietly for a moment and look around the park. And now, you’re resting.
Enjoy this quiet moment in the park.
